title: Rain and Cold Arrive in Rio: What to Expect in the Coming Days
seoTitle: Rain and Cold Arrive in Rio: What to Expect
subtitle: Alerta Rio indicates strong showers, moderate winds, and a temperature drop until Thursday
excerpt: Rio de Janeiro faces a week of intense rain, winds up to 52 km/h, and temperatures that could reach 13°C, according to Alerta Rio and Climatempo.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Alerta Rio issued warnings of moderate to heavy rain showers, winds up to 52 km/h, and a temperature drop that could reach 13°C on Thursday, generating significant public interest.

Rain and Temperature in the Next 48 Hours

On Monday (14), the sky will be overcast, with rain showers throughout the day and temperatures between 15°C and 23°C. On Tuesday (15), the weather will remain cloudy, with isolated showers during the early morning and a maximum of 25°C.

Forecast for Wednesday and Thursday

Wednesday (16) and Thursday (17) are expected to have light and isolated rain, with lows of 14°C and 13°C, respectively. Sunday (13) recorded a minimum of 18.1°C and a maximum of 24.9°C.

Wind and Safety Guidelines

The Rio Operations Center warned that gusts could reach between 40 km/h and 51.9 km/h. It is recommended to avoid staying under trees, metal roofs, outdoor sports, and loose objects in the yard. In case of intense rain with lightning, double your attention while driving, stay in a safe place, and avoid flooded areas.

Dark Spot in Copacabana

On Copacabana Beach, the State Environmental Institute (Inea) identified a dark spot on the sand strip near Post 5, possibly caused by mineral exposure after intense rainfall or pollution from storm drains. The situation is expected to persist until the forecast indicates a change in the rain pattern.

Impact on Daily Life

With the combination of cold, rain, and wind, the population should prepare for lower temperatures, wear appropriate clothing, and observe safety recommendations when moving on public roads and staying in outdoor areas.

With information from O GLOBO, O Dia, Terra.
